title: Field note 01: One file, ten findings, seven seams
description: The opening brief. A small owned source tree, a recorded finding, a source seam and the limit. Start here if you want the shape of the room before the detail.

title: Field note 02: The gate: no dossier, no publication
description: A finished run is not automatically a story. This note walks the publication gate: the records, the seam, the real target and the human sign-off.

title: Field note 03: The shape of the file
description: Twelve files, four languages and no binaries. A surface map can be useful without becoming a vulnerability claim. This note shows what the first finding actually records.

title: Field note 04: A seam is a place, not a change
description: The source is the first change surface. The safe path is baseline, edit one module, compare. This note explains what E-01 records and what it still does not prove.

title: Field note 05: The empty probe is evidence
description: Signal, empty, error, skipped, retry. The status is part of the finding. This note explains why a clean ledger includes the rows that found nothing.

title: Field note 06: Redact the value. Keep the finding.
description: A claim can be public without the secret that proved it. This note covers replacement at the source, the limits of a blur, and the edges that leak.

title: Field note 07: Confidence is not a probability
description: A confidence score is a recorded judgement, not a truth score. This note separates a direct observation from an inference and shows why the findings are never averaged.

title: Field note 08: The receipt is not the proof
description: The page carries a SHA-256 hash of the dossier. It ties the story to a record. It does not prove that every conclusion is correct. This note keeps the distinction clear.

title: Field note 09: A story is a selection
description: The public story is not a diary of every probe. It is an argued path through the strongest evidence. This note shows the five-part spine and what stays in the appendix.

title: Field note 10: What the room refuses
description: No exploits. No borrowed targets. No invented testimonials. No paid pack. The refusals are not a disclaimer at the bottom; they decide what can be published.

title: Scope and authorise a teardown
description: The boundary comes before the tool. A one-page scope, a written permission and a stop condition are what make the rest of the work publishable.

title: Run the evidence ladder
description: A repeatable sequence of probes, with statuses that tell you what is known, what is empty and what failed. Depth is earned, not assumed.

title: Redact secrets and private data
description: Publication is a second pass. Replace sensitive values at the source, keep the finding, and never rely on a blur that can be reversed.

title: Verify a dossier before it becomes public
description: The gate is a reading task. Check the claim, the locator, the confidence and the limit before the studio writes a single public word.

title: Turn a dossier into a story
description: A story is a selection, not a dump. Lead with scope, finding, seam, proof and limit, and let the appendix carry the rest.

title: Shoot the teardown video
description: Record the proof before you write the edit. A paper edit, real screen capture and a clear limit beat a cinematic montage with nothing behind it.

title: Publish a static evidence site
description: A portable page set with no database, no tracking scripts and no deployment surprise. Generate, inspect, link-check, then put it online.

title: Sell without hype
description: The offer follows the proof. One buyer, one painful workflow, one measurable deliverable and no invented social proof.
